synopsis: The booklet distinguishes code verification, which checks software implementation, from solution verification, which estimates numerical error in a particular run; verification is also distinct from validation against the real application [f14540, f10601]. Code verification uses problems with known exact answers once per software version, while solution verification refines time steps or spatial grids for each kind of run; a stopping-distance change from 41.9 m to 41.2 m after halving the time step illustrates numerical error that belongs in the uncertainty budget [f14541, f14542, f14543]. The credibility frameworks place code and solution verification before comparison with physical data, because unknown numerical artifacts can be mistaken for physics or tuned away [f14545, f14546]. A 2026 on-road round robin reported tool disagreements of 0.033 seconds and 0.314 metres despite prescribed triggering and braking, supporting the warning that a common scenario does not ensure equivalent simulator implementations [f14048, f6352]. Planning should therefore generate code and tool verification evidence, regression tests, solver checks and a verification report, supported by toolchain configuration management; model-verification exercises can begin before prototype arrival [f9727, f11107, f8034, f8238].
